slot.brief: Statements mixing All and Some with negatives; conclusions include possibility cases ('...being a possibility is true'), two of which look close.

stem:
Consider the statements to be true and decide which conclusion(s) logically follow.

**Statements:**
All falcons are birds.
Some falcons are nocturnal.
Some falcons are not nocturnal.
No nocturnal bird is silent.

**Conclusions:**
I. Some falcons being silent is a possibility.
II. All falcons being silent is a possibility.

verdicts.working: Nocturnal falcons are birds, so they cannot be silent. Since some falcons are not nocturnal, those falcons could be silent; thus I is possible. The known nocturnal falcons prevent all falcons from being silent, so II is not possible.

working:
A non-nocturnal falcon could be silent, so I is possible.
A nocturnal falcon must exist, and no nocturnal bird can be silent; hence II is impossible.
B and C wrongly allow all falcons to be silent; D wrongly rules out I.

Independent check: Nocturnal falcons are birds, so they cannot be silent. Since some falcons are not nocturnal, those falcons could be silent; thus I is possible. The known nocturnal falcons prevent all falcons from being silent, so II is not possible.
solution: Some falcons are not nocturnal, and they could be silent; hence I is possible. Some falcons are nocturnal, and since all falcons are birds, these falcons cannot be silent; hence II is impossible.
